title.en: The legislator as potter, the people as clay
title.nl: The legislator as potter, the people as clay

summary.fa: باستیا نشان می‌دهد پشت تحریف قانون یک تصویر از انسان ایستاده: موجودی منفعل و بی‌موتور که منتظر برنامهٔ قانون‌گذار عاقل است. او این تصویر را از زبان خودِ نویسندگان نقل می‌کند و بعد یک پرسش ساده می‌پرسد: اگر مردم این‌قدر ناتوان و نادان‌اند، چرا تمایلات سازمان‌دهندگان همیشه نیکوست؟
summary.en: Bastiat shows that behind the perversion of law stands a picture of man: a passive creature without a motor, waiting for the wise legislator’s plan. He quotes the picture in the authors’ own words and then asks a simple question: if people are so incapable and ignorant, how is it that the organizers’ own inclinations are always good?
summary.nl: Bastiat shows that behind the perversion of law stands a picture of man: a passive creature without a motor, waiting for the wise legislator’s plan. He quotes the picture in the authors’ own words and then asks a simple question: if people are so incapable and ignorant, how is it that the organizers’ own inclinations are always good?

text.fa: تصویر پنهان: به نوشتهٔ باستیا، دیدگاه جهانی پشت تحریف قانون «انسان را به‌عنوان کلیتی منفعل در نظر می‌گیرد که فاقد موتور است و منتظر عمل و برنامهٔ قانون‌گذار عاقل است».
text.en: The hidden picture: on Bastiat’s account the worldview behind the perversion of law "regards man as a passive whole lacking a motor, waiting for the wise legislator’s action and plan."
text.nl: The hidden picture: on Bastiat’s account the worldview behind the perversion of law "regards man as a passive whole lacking a motor, waiting for the wise legislator’s action and plan."

text.fa: و شواهدی که از خودشان نقل می‌کند: از روسو «قانون‌گذار مکانیکی است که ماشین را ابداع می‌کند»؛ از سن‌ژوست «قانون‌گذار برای آینده تعیین تکلیف می‌کند. این بر عهدهٔ اوست که خیر بشر را بخواهد، و بر عهدهٔ اوست که بشر را چنان بسازد که می‌خواهد»؛ از روبسپیر «کارکرد حکومت این است که توانایی‌های اخلاقی و فیزیکی ملت را در جهت هدفی که یک کشور آزاد برای آن به وجود آمده هدایت کند».
text.en: And the evidence he quotes from them: Rousseau, "the legislator is the mechanic who invents the machine"; Saint-Just, "the legislator decrees the future. It is for him to will the good of mankind, and for him to make mankind what he wants it to be"; Robespierre, "the function of government is to direct the moral and physical powers of the nation toward the end for which a free country was created."
text.nl: And the evidence he quotes from them: Rousseau, "the legislator is the mechanic who invents the machine"; Saint-Just, "the legislator decrees the future. It is for him to will the good of mankind, and for him to make mankind what he wants it to be"; Robespierre, "the function of government is to direct the moral and physical powers of the nation toward the end for which a free country was created."

text.fa: استعارهٔ مرکزی: «برای این روشنفکران و نویسندگان، رابطه میان مردم و قانون‌گذار همچون رابطه میان خاک و کوزه‌گر به نظر می‌آمد.» و تعجبی ندارد که نویسندگان قرن نوزدهم جامعه را «مخلوقی مصنوعی، ساخت نبوغ قانون‌گذار» می‌دیدند.
text.en: The central metaphor: "for these intellectuals and writers, the relation between the people and the legislator looked like the relation between clay and the potter." Small wonder, he adds, that nineteenth-century writers saw society as "an artificial creature, the product of the legislator’s genius."
text.nl: The central metaphor: "for these intellectuals and writers, the relation between the people and the legislator looked like the relation between clay and the potter." Small wonder, he adds, that nineteenth-century writers saw society as "an artificial creature, the product of the legislator’s genius."

text.fa: و تفاوتی که سوسیالیست نمی‌بیند: مخترع پیش از ماشین کامل مدلی می‌سازد، شیمی‌دان ماده‌ای را آزمایش می‌کند، کشاورز دانه و زمینی را. «اما چه تفاوتی این‌جا میان باغبان و درختانش، مخترع و ماشینش، شیمی‌دان و عناصرش، کشاورز و دانه‌هایش وجود دارد! سوسیالیست با صداقت تمام می‌انگارد که همین تفاوت میان او و انسان‌ها نیز موجود است.»
text.en: And the difference the socialist does not see: an inventor makes a model before the finished machine, a chemist tests a substance, a farmer a seed and a plot. "But what a difference there is between the gardener and his trees, the inventor and his machine, the chemist and his elements, the farmer and his seeds! The socialist in all sincerity imagines that the same difference holds between himself and human beings."
text.nl: And the difference the socialist does not see: an inventor makes a model before the finished machine, a chemist tests a substance, a farmer a seed and a plot. "But what a difference there is between the gardener and his trees, the inventor and his machine, the chemist and his elements, the farmer and his seeds! The socialist in all sincerity imagines that the same difference holds between himself and human beings."

text.fa: اعتراض باستیا به نویسندگان: «ای نویسندگان گران‌قدر! به یاد داشته باشید که این گل، این خاک و این کود که شما بی‌محابا به آن می‌پردازید، انسان است! آن‌ها هم‌نوعان شما هستند! آن‌ها انسان‌های آزاد و هوشمندی همانند شما هستند! آن‌ها نیز همانند شما از خداوند توانایی بررسی، برنامه‌ریزی، تفکر و قضاوت برای خودشان را دریافت کرده‌اند.»
text.en: Bastiat’s protest to the writers: "esteemed writers! Remember that this mud, this clay, this manure you handle so freely is man! They are your fellow creatures! They are free and intelligent human beings like you! They too have received from God the capacity to examine, to plan, to think and to judge for themselves."
text.nl: Bastiat’s protest to the writers: "esteemed writers! Remember that this mud, this clay, this manure you handle so freely is man! They are your fellow creatures! They are free and intelligent human beings like you! They too have received from God the capacity to examine, to plan, to think and to judge for themselves."

text.fa: و جایی که خشمش را نگه نمی‌دارد: «ای موجودات بی‌نوا! شما فکر می‌کنید که بسیار بزرگید! شمایی که انسانیت را بسی کوچک می‌انگارید! شمایی که آرزوی اصلاح هر چیز را دارید! چرا خود را اصلاح نمی‌کنید؟ چنین وظیفه‌ای شما را بس خواهد بود.»
text.en: And where he does not hold back: "poor creatures! You think you are so great! You who count humanity for so little! You who wish to reform everything! Why do you not reform yourselves? That task would be enough for you."
text.nl: And where he does not hold back: "poor creatures! You think you are so great! You who count humanity for so little! You who wish to reform everything! Why do you not reform yourselves? That task would be enough for you."

text.fa: نقد سمت دیگر: باستیا نقد آدام اسمیت را از «انسان سیستم» تکرار می‌کند — کسی که مردم را مهره‌هایی روی صفحهٔ شطرنج می‌بیند؛ و می‌افزاید قانون‌گذار برای رسیدن به هدفش باید تفاوت‌های انسانی را نادیده بگیرد، چون آن‌ها مانع برنامه‌اند.
text.en: A critique from the other side: Bastiat repeats Adam Smith’s criticism of "the man of system," who sees people as pieces on a chessboard; and he adds that the legislator must ignore human differences to reach his goal, since they obstruct the plan.
text.nl: A critique from the other side: Bastiat repeats Adam Smith’s criticism of "the man of system," who sees people as pieces on a chessboard; and he adds that the legislator must ignore human differences to reach his goal, since they obstruct the plan.

text.fa: و استدلال تقارن که ضربهٔ اصلی اوست: «افرادی که در جریان انتخابات بسیار دانا، با اخلاق و کامل بودند، اکنون گرایشی به این موارد ندارند… اگر افراد تا این حد ناتوان، بی‌اخلاق و ناآگاه هستند، دیگر چرا به افراد همانندشان حق داده شود که با چنین تأکید مشتاقانه‌ای به آن‌ها رأی دهند؟» و فشرده‌ترین صورتش: «اگر تمایلات طبیعی انسان‌ها تا این حد بد هستند که آزادی انسان‌ها موجب از بین رفتن امنیت شود، چگونه است که تمایلات این سازمان‌دهندگان همیشه نیکوست؟»
text.en: And the symmetry argument that is his main blow: "those who during the election were so wise, moral and perfect now show no such inclination… if people are so incapable, immoral and ignorant, why are people like them given the right to vote for them with such eager insistence?" And in its tightest form: "if men’s natural inclinations are so bad that their freedom would destroy security, how is it that the inclinations of these organizers are always good?"
text.nl: And the symmetry argument that is his main blow: "those who during the election were so wise, moral and perfect now show no such inclination… if people are so incapable, immoral and ignorant, why are people like them given the right to vote for them with such eager insistence?" And in its tightest form: "if men’s natural inclinations are so bad that their freedom would destroy security, how is it that the inclinations of these organizers are always good?"

text.fa: و پایان کتاب: فراخوانی برای آزادی و رد هر پیشنهادی که ترتیبات اجتماعی غیرطبیعی را بر مردم تحمیل می‌کند؛ از «قانون‌گذاران و خیرین» می‌خواهد «تمام سیستم‌ها را کنار بگذارند و آزادی را تجربه کنند».
text.en: And the book’s close: a call for liberty and a rejection of every proposal that imposes unnatural social arrangements on people; he asks "legislators and benefactors" to "throw aside all systems and try liberty."
text.nl: And the book’s close: a call for liberty and a rejection of every proposal that imposes unnatural social arrangements on people; he asks "legislators and benefactors" to "throw aside all systems and try liberty."

text.fa: استدلال تقارن باستیا یک پرسش واقعی است و در نظریهٔ انتخاب عمومی بعدها جدی گرفته شد، ولی خودش برای جایگزینش — این‌که بازار آزاد همین مسئله را ندارد — تقارن را به کار نمی‌برد. این مدخل نقد او را گزارش می‌کند، نه داوری می‌کند.
text.en: Bastiat’s symmetry argument raises a real question, later taken seriously in public-choice theory, but he does not apply the same symmetry to his own alternative — the claim that free markets do not face this problem. This entry reports his critique rather than adjudicating it.
